sources.notes: Road height is sampled from the existing approximately 78 m terrain raster and compressed to a 0.5 m interpolation tolerance relative to those samples; this is not road-surface survey accuracy. Station distances use the mapped trace, not an official length measurement. The saved start gate sets the simulation origin. Curbs and bend labels are geometry-based illustrations, not extracted from imagery or verified real curb locations; widths, heights and colours are assumed. Banking is unknown and assumed zero. Source border coordinates retain their separate feature-level licence; invalid cross-sections are interpolated. Imagery is an external display resource subject to provider terms; no image bytes are included.

supersedes.reason: The two pinned vertices form one transverse paint-line spur across the closing seam of the original boundary ring. The native review image and original/corrected local overlay show continuous road surface at this location. Their retained neighbours are within 1.1 m in the saved coordinates. Remove only these source vertices, retaining every other coordinate and original feature property. The closing duplicate follows the new first retained point; the exact original start point and full old ring reconstruct from the proof. The image has separate review rights. Remaining road limits and provisional route identity are unchanged and unverified.

borderInference.note: Reviewed deletion of the pinned source vertices only. Every retained coordinate and original border property is unchanged. Each paint-line group has a near return and bounded local excursion. Any numerical-loop group replaces an actual self-crossing with a chord at most two metres long and at most ten centimetres from every deleted point. The image supports local pavement interpretation but cannot resolve subpixel loops; this is not a new edge extraction or validation of the remaining source geometry.
